$comment: A public proposal, bridged from the API queue. Do not edit this file to resolve the proposal: change the record it targets and fill in `resolution`.

target.name: Does blocking Engrailed-1 activation (mechanotransduction/YAP inhibition) produce regeneration with appendages and native matrix in porcine or human skin, as it does in mouse?

summary: Porcine verteporfin study (Mascharak et al., Sci Transl Med 2025) reports scarless regeneration with neogenic follicles in red Duroc pig wounds — the large-animal test this question asks for
rationale: Mascharak, Griffin, Talbott ... Longaker, 'Inhibiting mechanotransduction prevents scarring and yields regeneration in a large animal model', Science Translational Medicine, 19 Feb 2025, doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.adt6387. Abstract: one-time verteporfin immediately after wounding prevented scarring and drove regeneration in red Duroc pig full-thickness wounds, with scRNA-seq and spatial proteomics of fibroblast and myeloid dynamics. This is from the originating group (Longaker), so it answers the porcine half of the question but not the 'unaffiliated group' condition in whatWouldResolve. Suggested edits: add the source and a claim at L3 (large animal, one group); move hrm:capability/dermal-architecture-regeneration-without-scar and fibrogenic-fibroblast-lineage-control from L2 to L3 with replication 0; leave the question open on the human and independent-replication halves. Surfaced by ChatGPT (GPT-5.6, web search) during the 2026-09-14 prediction run, then verified against Crossref and Europe PMC by Claude Code; not endorsed at figure level.
